observationsNotFindings: The fix took both remedies I offered rather than choosing one. I said the finding could be answered either by issuing a re-measured successor or by disclosing the historical scoping in the recording entry; v5 does both, supplying the successor and writing the historical framing into the artifact itself. That is the stronger answer, because the disclosure now travels with the artifact rather than living only in whichever entry records it.

My prediction in the D-172 verdict was that a re-measured v5 would carry the same ten obligations with the same flags and differ only in three governing pins and one cardinality. It held to the byte — zero obligation bodies changed. I record that as a tested result rather than a satisfying one: a matching prediction is the case where a reviewer is most likely to stop looking, so the obligation comparison here was run element-wise and field-wise rather than by spot-check.

My self-version pattern produced its first false positive: 'G07 v3 lands CLAUDE-G07-V2-B1' matched a rule meant to catch an artifact calling itself the wrong version, but 'G07 v3' names a different artifact. The pattern needs to distinguish a bare version token from one qualified by another artifact's name. Worth recording because the scan has caught three real findings in this session and a rule that over-matches will eventually be trusted less than it should be.

This artifact's recordedInputs contains no non-path keys, unlike the doctor-actor and permission chains which each carry a labelled commit id among their digests. Nothing turns on it, but it means the 24-of-24 count here is a complete file-digest verification with no exclusions.
